thread.title: Fresno State nonprofit adds members after board purge - NewsBreak

author: EdSource staff
title: Fresno State nonprofit adds members after board purge - NewsBreak
text:
By EdSource staff ,
1 days ago The Fresno State Foundation has appointed newcomers and implemented term limits after ousting five longstanding members and the resignation of three others, The Fresno Bee reported . Operating as a nonprofit independent of the university, the Fresno State Foundation controls more than $315 million for the campus, including scholarships and research funds.
According to The Bee, it had managed the philanthropic funds and research activity even though some of its board members lacked experience. Besides the Fresno State president, the board did not include university representation with any other school administrators, deans or faculty.
That lack of relevant experience was highlighted in a CSU review , which found that the foundation’s practices put it at risk of fraud . Fresno State President ​Saúl Jiménez-Sandoval, the sole university employee on the board, requested the review.
The board not having members representing the university will soon change. The board voted last week to include university representation to comply with state regulations and recommendations from the review.
Although not yet determined, the composition of the board will likely include one or two faculty members and a student representative, The Bee also reported .
This story was originally published by EdSource .
